checks.summary: ControlLoop.StopProcess wired to a real ProcessSupervisor{TermGrace:200ms} running a real shell child+grandchild in one process group (reusing supervisor_test.go's grandchildScript unmodified). ControlLoop.Apply(ControlImmediateStop) causes StopProcess to cancel the supervisor's context; measured elapsed (loop.Apply wall time) was >= TermGrace on every run, and both child_term and grandchild_term marker files (written only inside each process's own SIGTERM trap) exist, proving TERM was delivered to the whole group and escalation to KILL only happened after the grace period. checks.name: a10-control-agent-positive-and-negative
checks.summary: Negative (fail-closed): LatestRevision exceeding applied with LatestMode absent or an unknown string both cause the agent to apply domain.ControlImmediateStop (StopProcess invoked, journal state=terminated) rather than assume ControlAllow. Positive (through the real Service.Control/Heartbeat/LeaseKeeper/ControlAgent/reconciler pipeline, not a hand-built ControlProgress): with ControlAgent wired into LeaseKeeper, after two Ticks and one Reconciler.Tick fencing the now-stale Lease, VerificationReconciler.Tick reaches ControlVerified (changed=1). With no ControlAgent wired, the identical sequence leaves Verification pending (changed=0), because Heartbeat.AppliedRevision never reaches the stop revision and no ProcessObservation is ever reported. A pre-existing gap was found and fixed in service.go Control(): a found-but-runner-less CanonicalTarget left ControlTargetSnapshot.Target.RunnerID empty, so the verification reconciler's per-target RunnerObservation lookup (keyed by Target.RunnerID) could never match a real Runner; fixed by filling RunnerID from the Lease only when the canonical target does not already carry one (same fill-only-when-empty pattern as the existing canonicalizeTarget helper).

checks.name: a12-stop-mode-by-kind-matrix
checks.summary: 7 modes x 8 kinds = 56 cells, all through the real Service and a real OutboxDispatcher over a store. Measured finding: Capture and Checkpoint never construct a durable outbox effect and are gated purely by domain.Permit's per-kind table (pause-intake denies only intake, pause-claim denies only claim, graceful-stop allows only checkpoint). Claim, AcceptResult and all four OutboxDispatcher kinds (integration/promotion/preview-deploy/external-effect) construct an effect via domain.EffectFromPermit, which requires the current effective mode to be exactly ControlAllow -- so under every one of the six non-allow modes, including pause-intake and pause-claim, all of those are denied, even though the per-kind table alone would allow several of them under pause-intake/pause-claim. Allowed-cell totals: allow=8/8, pause-intake=2/8 (capture, checkpoint), pause-claim=2/8 (capture, checkpoint), graceful-stop=1/8 (checkpoint only), immediate-stop/emergency-stop/cancel=0/8 each (13/56 total). No sink invocation and no delivered outbox record for any denied cell; pause-claim, previously covered by no test at all, is now covered.
